name: Museu Lasar Segall
funding: Federal museum under IBRAM. The 2013 to 2015 renovation cost R$2.5M: R$1.5M from the National Culture Fund and R$1M from Petrobras.
records_note: Its site failed a certificate check and did not open; it is a federal museum under IBRAM, whose reports were not opened.

name: Museum Abteiberg
funding: City of Mönchengladbach Cultural Department, State of North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW); public municipal museum.
watch: Building by Hans Hollein. An early champion of Joseph Beuys, Fluxus and anti-market conceptual art.

name: Museum Arnhem
funding: Run by Stichting Musea Arnhem since 2014 on an annual Gemeente Arnhem subsidy (€2.6M in 2011).
watch: Reopened on 13 May 2022 after a delayed renovation. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: Museum Arnhem posts annual reports for 2012 to 2024, links full accounts, names its supervisory board, and names six funds undated.

name: Museum Beelden aan Zee
watch: The researcher's BNG, Aegon and other names come from 2018 and 2019 reports, so they are not current. BNG is state-owned; no protest found.
records_note: Its ANBI page posts annual reports 2017 to 2024, yearly accounts 2012 to 2025 and a named board; the 2024 report names about 30 funders.

name: Museum De Lakenhal
funding: Gemeente Leiden, Province of South Holland and OCW fund it. Its thanks page also names BankGiro Lottery, Mondriaan Fonds, Ammodo, BNG Cultuurfonds, VSBfonds and Fonds 21.
watch: The thanks page lists all donors since founding, including the tobacco-family Niemeijer Fonds, undated, so it is not counted. No protest found.
records_note: De Lakenhal posts annual reports for 2007 to 2025 that name its funds and partners, but shows no accounts and no board list.

name: Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens
funding: Flemish Government, Sint-Martens-Latem and the National Lottery. Partners include Christie's, Duvel, Puilaetco, Zwartopwit, Colora Gent, Jet Import and the Willame foundation.
watch: Belgian National Lottery money is a parliament-directed subsidy, so it counts as ordinary public funding.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2019 to 2025 and names its board and partners; the reports checked carry no financial statements.

name: Museum für Naturkunde
funding: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and State of Berlin joint financing.
watch: Leibniz Institute natural history museum; employee Kununu accounts detailing administrative workload.

name: Museum of Arts and Design
funding: $13.7M expenses (2023); private donors, NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs, exhibition patrons such as Sarah Arison and Duggal.
watch: Ex-CFO sued in Mar 2024, saying she was fired for flagging the director's expenses. No institutional donor roster is published.
records_note: Annual reports for 2008 and 2009 and audited accounts for 2013 to 2019 are on its site; no donor list; trustees are listed.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art and Design (MCAD)
funding: Run by De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde; Art Circle patrons and benefit auctions (2018, 15 Nov 2025) with Leon Gallery as auction partner.
watch: No donor list is published. No controversy found.
records_note: Its Support, About and Downloads pages post no reports, accounts, named donors or board; it sits under De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA)
funding: AUD 28M. Australia Council for the Arts, NSW Government, Telstra, Qantas, private benefactors.
watch: Sydney harbourfront museum with large Australian corporate sponsors.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago (MCA)
funding: Individual donations, board giving, Northern Trust, BMO Harris, Bank of America.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego
funding: Expenses $13.7M (FY2025); $40M+ endowment, trustees, banks (JPMorgan, Northern Trust, Bank of America), Westfield UTC, KPBS.
watch: The 1990s pergola dispute was about architecture, not funding.
records_note: No annual reports found; audited statements 2016 to 2025 and Form 990s are on its site, corporate partners show as logos, and trustees are listed.
